issue.title: Improve text format handling in Amazon Lambda

body: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/46203 is a quick fix but I assume that at some point we'll need better content type handling in Amazon Lambda

@geoand Thank you for your help!

> I assume that at some point we'll need better content type handling in Amazon Lambda

I took a look at the commit and the content type detection looks a little shaky which is probably what you are referring to. There are basically two ways it could fail:

1. Detecting binary content as text
2. Detecting text content as binary

While this issue arose from point 1, I wonder if there are any serious drawbacks from 2. It looks to me like the response would just get base-64-encoded, and Lambda would then decode it back, but that would still get the response to the client.

If I'm not missing anything here, it seems that the `isText` method should return true only if it is absolutely certain and false in other cases. 

My idea would be to check whether the mime type starts with `text/` and then maybe just check against a predefined set of commonly used text mime types that do not start with `text/`, like `application/json`, `image/svg+xml` and `application/xml`.
If you have a case showing the current implementation stumbles, we can certainly look into using something like what you mention

I don't have any specific use case in mind currently. It is just an idea to make the implementation more resilient in cases where nieche / custom mime types are used.

If you take a look at the [list of mime types](https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml), there are several with xml in their name, and at least `application/vnd.wap.wbxml` should be treated as binary data. Also, new ones can be added at any time that will be falsely identified as text with the current check and users might try to use custom, non standard mime types not knowing that it will break their responses.
